es.summary: Clopidogrel es un inhibidor irreversible del receptor P2Y12 de ADP que reduce la agregación plaquetaria.
key_points: Se usa para prevenir eventos trombóticos tras síndrome coronario agudo o colocación de stent.
Comienza a actuar en 2‑3 días; efecto máximo a 5‑7 días.
No debe combinarse con anticoagulantes sin indicación clara.

mechanism: Bloquea irreversiblemente el receptor P2Y12 en plaquetas.
Impide la activación de la glicoproteína IIb/IIIa.
Reduce la unión del fibrinógeno y la agregación plaquetaria.
indications: Prevención secundaria de infarto de miocardio y accidente cerebrovascular.
Después de implantación de stent coronario (p. ej., stent metálico o farmacológico).
contraindications: Hipersensibilidad conocida al clopidogrel o a sus excipientes.
Hemorragia activa o trastorno hemorrágico grave.
Uso concomitante de anticoagulantes orales sin indicación específica.
interactions: Aumento del sangrado con AINES, warfarina, heparina o DOACs.
Inhibidores de CYP2C19 (p. ej., omeprazol) reducen la activación de clopidogrel.
Inductores de CYP2C19 (p. ej., rifampicina) pueden disminuir su eficacia.
nursing_care: Evaluar signos de sangrado antes de administrar (hematomas, hematoquecia, epistaxis).
Obtener hemograma completo y plaquetas antes y durante la terapia.
Retener la dosis y notificar al médico si ocurre sangrado activo o hemoglobina ↓ 2 g/dL.
Verificar uso concomitante de AINES o anticoagulantes.
Documentar hora de la última dosis antes de procedimientos invasivos.
patient_teaching: Tomar la tableta a la misma hora cada día, sin masticar.
Reportar cualquier sangrado inusual, sangre en heces o vómito.
Evitar el uso de aspirina o ibuprofeno sin consultar al médico.
Informar al dentista y cirujano antes de procedimientos invasivos.

outcomes: No se presentarán episodios de sangrado evidenciado durante la hospitalización.
Hemoglobina y hematocrito se mantendrán dentro de rangos normales (Hb > 12 g/dL).

interventions.action: Evaluar diariamente signos de sangrado activo (p. ej., hematomas, hematoquecia).
interventions.rationale: Detección temprana permite intervención o suspensión del fármaco.
Identifica disminución de plaquetas o hemoglobina que indique sangrado.

interventions.action: Revisar historial de uso de AINES, anticoagulantes y suplementos que aumenten el riesgo hemorrágico.
interventions.rationale: Previene interacciones que potencien el sangrado.

interventions.action: Retener clopidogrel y notificar al médico si se detecta sangrado activo o Hb ↓ 2 g/dL.
interventions.rationale: Evita empeoramiento del sangrado y permite ajuste terapéutico.

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre signos de sangrado y cuándo buscar ayuda médica.
interventions.rationale: Fomenta la autovigilancia y la búsqueda oportuna de atención.

en.summary: Clopidogrel is an irreversible inhibitor of the ADP P2Y12 receptor that reduces platelet aggregation.
key_points: Used to prevent thrombotic events after acute coronary syndrome or stent placement.
Begins to act in 2‑3 days; peak effect at 5‑7 days.
Should not be combined with anticoagulants without clear indication.

mechanism: Irreversibly blocks the P2Y12 receptor on platelets.
Reduces fibrinogen binding and platelet aggregation.
indications: Secondary prevention of myocardial infarction and stroke.
After coronary stent implantation (e.g., metallic or drug-eluting stent).
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to clopidogrel or its excipients.
Active bleeding or severe bleeding disorder.
Concurrent use of oral anticoagulants without specific indication.
interactions: Increased bleeding with NSAIDs, warfarin, heparin or DOACs.
CYP2C19 inhibitors (e.g., omeprazole) reduce clopidogrel activation.
CYP2C19 inducers (e.g., rifampin) may decrease efficacy.
nursing_care: Assess for bleeding signs before administration (hematomas, melena, epistaxis).
Obtain CBC and platelets before and during therapy.
Hold dose and notify provider if active bleeding or hemoglobin ↓ 2 g/dL.
Verify concurrent use of NSAIDs or anticoagulants.
Document time of last dose before invasive procedures.
patient_teaching: Take the tablet at the same time each day, do not chew.
Report any unusual bleeding, blood in stool or vomit.
Avoid aspirin or ibuprofen without consulting the provider.
Inform dentist and surgeon before invasive procedures.

outcomes: No bleeding episodes will occur during hospitalization.
Hemoglobin and hematocrit will remain within normal ranges (Hb > 12 g/dL).

interventions.action: Assess daily for active bleeding signs (e.g., hematomas, melena).
interventions.rationale: Early detection allows intervention or drug discontinuation.
Identifies platelet or hemoglobin drop indicating bleeding.

interventions.action: Review history of NSAID, anticoagulant, and supplement use that increase hemorrhagic risk.
Hold clopidogrel and notify provider if active bleeding or Hb ↓ 2 g/dL.
interventions.rationale: Prevents worsening bleeding and allows therapeutic adjustment.

interventions.action: Educate patient on bleeding signs and when to seek medical help.

key_points.0.quote: One of the most common uses for antiplatelets is therapy after a client has an acute coronary syndrome and/or a coronary artery stent placed.

sections.mechanism.1.quote: Eptifibatide inhibits the GPIIbIIIa receptor on the platelet surface, preventing activation by von Willebrand’s factor and fibrinogen.

sections.mechanism.2.quote: Eptifibatide inhibits the GPIIbIIIa receptor on the platelet surface, preventing activation by von Willebrand’s factor and fibrinogen.

sections.indications.0.quote: One of the most common uses for antiplatelets is therapy after a client has an acute coronary syndrome and/or a coronary artery stent placed.

sections.indications.1.quote: To reduce the rate of myocardial infarction and stroke in clients with recent myocardial infarction, stroke, or established peripheral artery disease

sections.indications.2.quote: One of the most common uses for antiplatelets is therapy after a client has an acute coronary syndrome and/or a coronary artery stent placed.

sections.contraindications.1.quote: A history of bleeding complications, such as intracranial hemorrhage or gastrointestinal bleeding, may be considered a contraindication to further antiplatelet therapy, depending on the circumstances and the drug.

sections.adverse_effects.0.quote: Subsequently, gastrointestinal effects are a major adverse effect, and it has additive gastrointestinal bleeding risk beyond its antiplatelet effect.

sections.adverse_effects.2.quote: The major side effect of eptifibatide is profound thrombocytopenia.

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: If acute effects of aspirin are needed, such as during a heart attack, it is recommended that aspirin be chewed and swallowed for faster absorption (Mayo Clinic, n.d.).

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Some symptoms of bleeding are blood in the stool; dark, tarry-appearing stools; blood in the urine; epistaxis; gingival bleeding; very severe headache; coffee-ground emesis; and hemoptysis.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Concomitant medications that further increase bleeding risk such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (e.g., ibuprofen and naproxen) or antiplatelet agents (e.g., aspirin) may also be considered contraindicated with antiplatelet medications.
